15 COMMON ORDER:

- 
In all these writ petitions, the petitioners are either residing in the properties abutting the road or conducting business in the properties abutting the road.

The petitioners have filed the present writ petitions, aggrieved by the proposed action of the 2nd respondent in taking up the road widening from the existing 40 to 60 feet from Tenali road of Mangalagiri town.

It is submitted that the petitioners are apprehending pressure from the 2nd respondent in yielding to the demand of the 2nd respondent in offering TDR bonds as the only solution for acquiring the petitioners' property.

2. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are all small traders and apart from the property over which they are residing they have no other property or other livelihood.

It is submitted that the petitioners are now exposed to the demands of the 2nd respondent and the 2nd respondent without issuing any notice has resorted to marking the petitioners' property for the purpose of road widening.

In that regard, whenever the petitioners approached the 2nd respondent, they were orally informed to accept the TDR bonds offered by the 2nd respondent in pursuance of G.O.Ms.No.119, dated 28.03.2017.

It is submitted that the petitioners are not willing to accept the TDR bonds, as the same is not commensurative alternative to The Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the petitioners would not be adequately compensated in the event the respondent authorities do not follow the Act 30 of 2013.
3. The 2nd respondent has filed a detailed counter along with Council Resolution and the newspaper clippings relating to the proposed road widening.

It is submitted in the counter that the 2nd respondent is in the process of implementing the zonal development plan and also keeping in view the changed circumstances in the Tadepalli Municipality, the requirement of widening the road from 40 feet to 60 feet was considered essential about 20 years ago.
However, the same could not materialize on account of various reasons.

It is also submitted that the services of RITES were engaged for conducting comprehensive mobility plan for Mangalagiri-Tadepalli Municipal Corporation for the 2nd respondent area and a proposal to widen the road from existing 2 lanes to 4 lanes were also submitted.
4.
It is submitted that the Zonal Development Plan would have to match the phase of development and traffic as such the respondents have to essentially widen the existing road.

It is further submitted that the 2nd respondent shall follow the applicable provisions of the Municipal Corporation Act i.e., Sections 146 and 147 of the A.P. Municipal Act, 1955 and A.P. Building Rules,
2017, for arriving at compensation for the land acquired for road widening.

It is also stated in the counter that meetings were conducted with the property owners, whose properties were affected in Goli Venkateswara Rao vs The State Of Ap on 31 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163144118/
11 road widening and some of the property owners had given consent by accepting T.D.R. certificates.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is submitted that the writ petitions are filed with an apprehension, without issuance of any notice and that no cause of action has arisen for the petitioners to file the present writ petitions.
5.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri A.S.C.Bose, learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 2nd respondent.

6. Perused the record.
7.
Admittedly, the 2nd respondent is in the process of widening of the road from the existing 40 feet to 60 feet, as per the Zonal Development Plan notified vide G.O.Ms.No.687, MA, dated 30.12.2006.
It is also evident that the petitioners' properties are likely to be affected in the road widening process.

As stated by the learned Standing Counsel for the 2 nd respondent that some of the property owners have expressed their consent for accepting the T.D.R bonds and that the 2nd respondent would also negotiate with the petitioners for offering T.D.R bonds in lieu of their properties.

8. Considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners have never expressed their consent for accepting T.D.R bonds and have personally visited the office of the 2nd respondent and requested the Commissioner to consider their cases for grant of compensation under The Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The claims of the petitioners were not considered and they were called upon to attend the proposed meeting for negotiation.
The procedure contemplated Section 146 of the Municipal Corporation Act, deals with the acquisition of immovable property by agreement.
Section 147 prescribes the procedure, when immovable property cannot be acquired by agreement.

9. The petitioners, if they are not accepting for the T.D.R bonds offered by the 2nd respondent, the only option left for the 2nd respondent will be to invoke the procedure contemplated under Section 147 of the Municipal Corporation Act and the property of the petitioners would have to be acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.

The only option for the respondents would be to follow the procedure under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
10. Considering the same, the writ petitions are disposed off, making it clear to the 2nd respondent that, if any of the petitioners submit in writing their dissent for accepting the T.D.R. bonds offered,
the respondents shall have to essentially follow the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 11. With these observations, the writ petitions are disposed off.
No order as to costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
- 
In all these writ petitions, the petitioners are either residing in the properties abutting the road or conducting business in the properties abutting the road.
The petitioners have filed the present writ petitions, aggrieved by the proposed action of the 2nd respondent in taking up the road widening from the existing 40 to 60 feet from Tenali road of Mangalagiri town.
In that regard, whenever the petitioners approached the 2nd respondent, they were orally informed to accept the TDR bonds offered by the 2nd respondent in pursuance of G.O.Ms.No.119, dated 28.03.2017.
It is further submitted that the 2nd respondent shall follow the applicable provisions of the Municipal Corporation Act i.e., Sections 146 and 147 of the A.P. Municipal Act, 1955 and A.P. Building Rules,
2017, for arriving at compensation for the land acquired for road widening.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is submitted that the petitioners are now exposed to the demands of the 2nd respondent and the 2nd respondent without issuing any notice has resorted to marking the petitioners' property for the purpose of road widening.
It is also submitted that the petitioners would not be adequately compensated in the event the respondent authorities do not follow the Act 30 of 2013.
It is submitted in the counter that the 2nd respondent is in the process of implementing the zonal development plan and also keeping in view the changed circumstances in the Tadepalli Municipality, the requirement of widening the road from 40 feet to 60 feet was considered essential about 20 years ago.
8. Considering the submissions of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the petitioners have never expressed their consent for accepting T.D.R bonds and have personally visited the office of the 2nd respondent and requested the Commissioner to consider their cases for grant of compensation under The Right of Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
The claims of the petitioners were not considered and they were called upon to attend the proposed meeting for negotiation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The procedure contemplated Section 146 of the Municipal Corporation Act, deals with the acquisition of immovable property by agreement.
Section 147 prescribes the procedure, when immovable property cannot be acquired by agreement.
opennyai_summary.decision:
9. The petitioners, if they are not accepting for the T.D.R bonds offered by the 2nd respondent, the only option left for the 2nd respondent will be to invoke the procedure contemplated under Section 147 of the Municipal Corporation Act and the property of the petitioners would have to be acquired under the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act.
The only option for the respondents would be to follow the procedure under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
10. Considering the same, the writ petitions are disposed off, making it clear to the 2nd respondent that, if any of the petitioners submit in writing their dissent for accepting the T.D.R. bonds offered,
the respondents shall have to essentially follow the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
11. With these observations, the writ petitions are disposed off.
No order as to costs.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
